answer: A stake-weighted reputation registry makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent locks collateral before joining, and misbehavior slashes the deposit. New identities start on a low ridge of trust and climb only through verified work, so spawning fake agents costs more than any fraud returns. Like timber inspected before it bears weight, each agent's history is checked by peers before its attestations count. A canyon thus opens between cheap pseudonyms and trusted participants: attackers face real capital loss per identity, while honest agents build standing that cannot be bought in bulk.
